headline: Southborough secured a $3.9 million state culvert grant, authorized a $105,000 police drone package, and saw Neary roof bids come in under budget.
synopsis: In June 2026, Southborough secured a major fiscal victory when the state awarded nearly $3.9 million in culvert grants, eliminating the need to issue municipal debt authorized at Town Meeting. The Select Board narrowly approved using $105,000 in police department salary surplus to purchase an Axon drone package despite debate over bypassing Town Meeting appropriations. School infrastructure advanced on two fronts as Neary Elementary roof bids came in at $2.8 million—well below the $4.5 million authorized—and the regional district finalized a $7.115 million bond sale for high school athletic facilities. Wastewater planning along Route 9 slowed after the Wastewater Study Committee unanimously rejected $30,000 for an economic financing study until a viable facility site is identified. Meanwhile, town boards finalized dates for upcoming town meetings and reviewed revised Community Preservation Act applications for trail, park, and golf course improvements.

top_items.title: Select Board approves $105,000 police drone package
top_items.why: In a 3-2 vote, the Select Board authorized using year-end police department salary surplus to purchase a five-year drone package rather than seeking Town Meeting approval.
top_items.body: Police Chief Ryan Newell requested bottom-line spending of surplus personnel funds from unfilled positions to purchase an Axon drone package, offset by a $20,000 contribution from Fay School. While the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed the program as an immediate safety priority, Select Board members debated whether funding major capital equipment through operating surplus bypassed proper town vetting before approving the purchase 3-2.

top_items.title: State awards nearly $3.9 million for town culverts
top_items.why: Southborough received a $3.9 million state culvert grant, allowing the town to avoid issuing $3.9 million in previously authorized borrowing.
top_items.body: The Select Board announced that Southborough received nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program. The state funding will pay for town-wide culvert infrastructure replacements, replacing debt previously approved by Town Meeting and sparing the town from taking on new borrowing.

top_items.title: Regional School Committee approves $7.1 million athletic bond sale
top_items.why: Favorable market conditions allowed the district to downsize its borrowing from $7.735 million to $7.115 million for the Algonquin athletic complex.
top_items.body: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee unanimously approved the issuance and sale of general obligation bonds to Loop Capital Markets LLC at a 3.07 percent true interest cost. The financing covers construction of the high school athletic complex and amenities building, with debt service running through June 2039.

top_items.title: Neary roof bids come in at $2.8 million
top_items.why: Competitive bids for replacing the Neary Elementary School roof came in at $2.8 million, substantially under the $4.5 million appropriated by Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The School Committee received favorable bid results for the Neary Elementary School roof replacement, which will start construction in late June with built-in contingency funds. Concurrently, the Elementary School Building Committee kicked off a $165,000 feasibility study with Tappé Architects to evaluate broader renovation and addition options for the facility.

top_items.title: Wastewater committee halts $30,000 Route 9 economic study
top_items.why: The Wastewater Study Committee voted 0-5 against spending $30,000 for a consultant financial study, postponing a planned fall Town Meeting article.
top_items.body: Although the Select Board voted 4-1 earlier in the month to authorize $30,000 in unused Economic Development Committee funds for a MassDevelopment financing analysis, the Wastewater Study Committee unanimously rejected funding the study. Members concluded it was premature to spend money modeling a District Improvement Financing (DIF) district before confirming whether a viable site for a treatment and disposal plant exists.

top_items.title: Trails Committee scales back Peninsula Trail Phase 2 request
top_items.why: To fit within funding constraints after bids exceeded estimates, the committee voted to pursue CPA funds solely for a pedestrian footbridge, eliminating a proposed boardwalk.
top_items.body: Facing combined bridge and boardwalk bids of approximately $630,000, the Trails Committee adjusted its approach to seek roughly $440,000 to $450,000 for the bridge and abutments while rerouting the trail onto dry ground. The Conservation Commission and Recreation Commission both voted unanimously to support the committee's updated Community Preservation Act application.

top_items.title: Select Board sets dates for upcoming Town Meetings
top_items.why: The Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027.
top_items.body: The Select Board reviewed the municipal and school calendars to establish Town Meeting dates. The board voted 5-0 to set the Fall Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10:00 AM.
